15.0.0.en: The Spirit of God came upon a prophet named Azariah, and upon his father Oded, and commanded them to go to meet Asa and the people of the kingdom of Judah. Here we see the coming of the Holy Spirit in the Old Testament as temporary, to accomplish a divine work, and here it is the declaration of a prophecy and the strengthening of the prophet so that he might face the king and all the people with courage; whereas in the New Testament the Holy Spirit dwells permanently in the believers, through the sacrament of the Holy Myron. And if He came here so that all the speech might be with God's precision, our submission in the New Testament to the Holy Spirit makes our words and our works from God.

15.0.1.en: Azariah stood and said to Asa and the people of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin that God is with them, on condition that they remain holding fast to Him, but if they turn away from Him, He will abandon them; that is, man's will is necessary for his salvation and for his enjoying God's care.

15.0.2.en: And we notice the timing that God chose for sending Azariah, namely after His people's victory over Zerah the Cushite, so that they would not be absorbed in the victory and the spoil and become proud and forget God, and the devil attack them and make them fall. The continuance of victory is bound to the continuance of cleaving to God and relying on Him.

15.1.0.en: Azariah the prophet reminds the people that many days had passed over the children of Israel in which they neglected the worship of God, and their priests and their teachings, and likewise the commandments of God and His law. This was clear in the era of the Judges and recurred at various times, such as the days of King Saul and also the ten tribes when they broke away at the hand of Jeroboam. And the prophet's words apply to any period in which the people of God turn away from Him.

15.1.1.en: And when the people forsook God, their enemies troubled them, so they cried out to God, who hastened to them and rescued them, declaring that they were His people and under His care.

15.1.2.en: The people fluctuated between the worship of God and neglecting it, so they lost God's care and, consequently, reassurance and security, and were greatly exposed to the attacks of enemies, in addition to the conflicts and internal problems among the people, so they had no rest or peace; and because of the evils of the people of God, He allowed many nations to rise against them, and they killed many of them and even enslaved and humbled them. That is, God allowed the wicked to trouble His people so that they would repent and return to Him, and not perish.

15.2.0.en: The summary of the prophecy and its purpose, which Azariah declared to the people, is that they should be strong in the Lord, so as to be rid of evil, do good and worship God, and God would reward them with great rewards in this age and in the age to come.

15.2.1.en: Hold fast to your spiritual rule and your worship of God, whatever your preoccupations or the problems you are going through. By this you secure God's care and support for you, and He will even fight for you and let you enjoy His fellowship.

15.2.3.en: 8- And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the LORD, that was before the porch of the LORD.

15.2.4.en: 9- And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the LORD his God was with him. 10- So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa. 11- And they offered unto the LORD the same time, of the spoil which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep. 12- And they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul; 13- That whosoever would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman. 14- And they sware unto the LORD with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets. 15- And all Judah rejoiced at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the LORD gave them rest round about. 16- And also concerning Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped it, and burnt it at the brook Kidron. 17- But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. 18- And he brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.

15.2.5.en: 19- And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.

15.3.0.en: Asa responded quickly to the word of God through the mouth of Oded the prophet and his son Azariah, and removed the pagan altars, which he had begun to remove at the beginning of his reign, whether from the lands of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, or from the cities he had taken from Israel, which lie north of the kingdom of Judah in the mountain of Ephraim. These may be the cities that his father Abijah had taken (ch. 13:19). This is the first reform in the series of Asa's reforms.

15.3.1.en: The second of Asa's reforms is the renewal of the altar of the Lord that was before the porch, that is, the court in the temple, and this altar is the bronze altar. Perhaps it had fallen into ruin, or suffered some damage, during the period of neglect of worship in the temple, in the days of Rehoboam and Abijah, a period of thirty-five years (17 years of Rehoboam's reign + 3 years of Abijah's reign + 15 years from the beginning of Asa's reign until this time (v. 10).)

15.4.0.en: The third reform is the gathering of the believers, not only in the kingdom of Judah but also those in the kingdom of Israel, that is, the ten tribes, who heard of the renewal of the worship of God in His temple, so they left their lands and came to Jerusalem to take part in the worship of God and encouraged their brethren in the kingdom of Judah.

15.4.1.en: How beautiful it is to look for those who love God, to befriend them, so that you are encouraged by them and encourage them in the worship of God. In addition to this is the importance of your friendship with the saints, who have completed their striving on earth and live in the love of God. All this pushes you great steps forward on the way to the Kingdom.

15.5.0.en: The fourth reform that Asa carried out is offering worship and love of God in abundance, for Asa and his people did not cling to the spoil they had brought from Zerah the Cushite, but offered from it on God's altar seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep. Thus the picture of the intense love that Solomon offered at the dedication of the temple of God is renewed (ch. 7:5).

15.6.0.en: The fifth reform is making a covenant with God to seek Him with all their heart, that is, not to ask anything from the pagan gods and not to rely on their own strength, and whoever does not seek the Lord and takes refuge in idols is put to death. We notice here the repeated seeking of the Lord by Asa in the Second Book of Chronicles from (ch. 14-16), which contains forty-eight verses, in which the seeking of the Lord is repeated five times, and this shows Asa's care for prayer and taking refuge in God.

15.6.1.en: And the people swore to God to worship Him and seek Him alone; indeed, they shouted and used the trumpets and the horns, declaring their faith in God and their holding fast to Him.

15.6.2.en: And they rejoiced greatly at this oath and covenant, because they sought God of their own will with all their hearts, that is, the king did not pressure them in this covenant. This shows God's concern for the human will, so God answered them and they felt His presence with them and His blessing, and He gave them rest from the attacks of enemies and peace in their hearts.

15.7.0.en: These verses are recorded and were explained in (1 Kgs 15:13-15), and we see in them Asa's sixth reform, which is the removal of Queen Maachah and the destruction of her idol and her grove, for he took care to reform the royal palace, that is, his own house, and we see his holding fast to God more than his concern for his family relationships, "We ought to obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29). This is great courage, because Maachah was a strong, dominating personality.

15.8.0.en: Because of Asa's goodness and his reforms, God blessed him, so he spent thirty-five years of his reign in rest, which is a long period that shows God's love for him. Here Asa resembles Solomon his forefather, who took care to build the temple of God, so He gave him rest and subdued the nations to him, as the Holy Bible says, "When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him" (Prov 16:7). The Holy Bible testifies here that Asa's heart was perfect before God (v. 17), so he is counted among the good kings, but it was not like the heart of David his father (1 Kgs 15:3), for David is the perfect measure of the love of God. Asa walked in the way of David's perfection, but only in part, and David was perfect, yet a man with his faults, such as the sin concerning Uriah the Hittite (2 Sam 12:9) and the numbering of the people (2 Sam 24); he is the best king who appeared on the throne of the children of Israel, for when he sinned he repented, and God forgave him; whereas Asa walked in the ways of perfection but his repentance was not complete, for he listened to Oded and Azariah but did not listen to Hanani the seer (ch. 16). Asa's fall and then his death

16.0.0.en: When Asa fell into relying on men and forsook God, the Lord sent Hanani the seer to rebuke him, and he said to him: Because you relied on the king of Syria to stop Baasha's attack, instead of relying on God, you have lost something great, namely the escape of the king of Syria from your hand; for God's plan was to subdue him to you, so that you would become one of the strongest nations in the region in which you live. Asa's sin is weakness of faith and doubt in God; he feared Baasha and began to look for someone to support him and took refuge in Syria. And Asa's fear drove him to dig a pit to hide in from the face of Baasha, and Jeremiah the prophet referred to it (Jer 41:9).

16.1.0.en: Hanani reminded King Asa that God had delivered into his hand the very great army of Zerah, armed with chariots and various weapons, because he relied on God, so he did not care about the strength of the Cushites and the Libyans who were with Zerah. And here is a clear rebuke: Why, Asa, did you go back on your faith and your reliance on God, in which you walked with Zerah, and then abandon it with Baasha?!

16.2.0.en: Hanani made clear to Asa that God is the searcher of hearts and reins and seeks His children who believe in Him, to strengthen and fortify them before all the afflictions they meet; but because you, Asa, have abandoned your faith, God will punish you by raising wars against you from your enemies.

16.3.0.en: Sadly, Asa did not submit to the voice of God and repent of his sin; on the contrary, he punished Hanani the seer, who had conveyed God's words to him, and threw him into prison to silence the voice of God, that is, the voice of Hanani. And he troubled the believers in God who supported Hanani and tried to push Asa to repentance, and wronged them instead of thanking them.

16.3.1.en: Accept the voice of God through the mouth of one who reproves you and do not be annoyed at him because of your pride, for God in His love sent these to you so that you might repent and not perish in eternal torment.

16.3.2.en: And so we find that Asa fell into a series of sins, which are:

16.3.3.en: 1- Weakness of his faith and his not taking refuge in God.

16.3.4.en: 2- Fear of men, that is, of Baasha.

16.3.5.en: 3- Taking refuge in a pagan king, the king of Syria, instead of God.

16.3.6.en: 4- Paying a bribe to Syria of silver and gold from the house of the Lord, instead of adding to the treasury of the house of the Lord from the spoil he obtained from his victories over his enemies by the power of God, as happened when he triumphed over Zerah and took much spoil from him.

16.3.7.en: 5- He encouraged the king of Syria to commit a sin, which is breaking his covenant with Baasha.

16.3.8.en: 6- He made a pagan king fight his cousins, who are the kingdom of Israel, and in this way his own kingdom also was exposed to danger from the king of Syria, who could break his covenant with him at any time.

16.3.9.en: 7- He refused to submit to God's word through Hanani.

16.3.10.en: 8- He wronged the one who declared the truth to him, namely Hanani, and a number of believers in his kingdom, whom he troubled.

17.0.s.en: (1) The greatness of Jehoshaphat because of his holding fast to the commandments of the Lord

17.0.0.en: After the death of Asa his son Jehoshaphat reigned over the kingdom of Judah, and took care to fortify his kingdom against the kingdom of Israel, because of its deviation from the worship of God and its worship of idols. So he placed an army in the fortified cities of Judah and appointed governors to manage them with strength, and he also appointed governors in the cities that Asa had taken from the kingdom of Israel, situated in the tribe of Ephraim. His intention was not to fight the kingdom of Israel but to protect his kingdom from the evils of Israel.

17.1.0.en: Jehoshaphat relied for his strength on God, so he took care of the worship of God in His temple and held fast to His commandments, like David his father, who was the measure of life with God, and he did not slip into the worship of the pagan gods, the most important of which was the god Baal, or the Baalim, whose worship had spread in the kingdom of Israel.

17.2.0.en: Because of Jehoshaphat's cleaving to the worship of God, God established his kingdom, so peace and stability prevailed, and his people submitted to him and also brought him gifts.

17.3.0.en: Jehoshaphat's reforms did not stop at his worship of God, but he took courage and removed the worship of idols that was carried on at the high places, whether the groves, or the altars, or the idols; and this matter was extremely difficult, because the people had become attached to these evil forms of worship.

17.3.1.en: And although Asa had removed these forms of worship set up at the high places, and took care to walk in the way of the Lord with exactness, that is, he walked in the way of spiritual perfection, he did not follow the people's conduct closely, so some of them returned to this worship, especially at the end of Asa's life, when he fell ill and refused to take refuge in God and did not listen to God's word through the mouth of Hanani the seer, but imprisoned him.

17.3.2.en: Your relationship with God is the foundation of your success in all your works and your life. May you make God your only goal, and order your life in a way that does not conflict with His will, and in this way you will succeed in everything to which your hands reach out.

17.4.s.en: (2) His teaching of the Law to the people

17.4.0.en: Jehoshaphat was not content with removing the pagan worship at the high places, but also took care of the religious instruction of his people, that they might love God and fear Him and be rid of any traces of pagan worship, such as the images in their houses, or any evil customs they had learned from the surrounding nations. So he sent five of his princes to teach the people, and these had civil authority, that is, so that the people would understand that these teachings were approved by the king, and the people would respect God and the command of their king.

17.5.0.en: Jehoshaphat also sent two priests and with them nine Levites, whom he chose, perhaps because of their distinction in the Law and their excellence in the ability to teach, and they went about the cities of the kingdom of Judah teaching the people the Law of God, having with them a copy of the Law of God, of which one copy was kept with the king and another in the house of the Lord.

17.5.1.en: From this Jehoshaphat's wisdom appears, who was convinced that any revival in his kingdom must be built on the people's knowledge of the Law of God and walking by it.

17.5.2.en: Take care to teach your children and loved ones the word of God, in the proper way, for this is your responsibility, and God will hold you accountable for it, and this is more fitting for you than complaining about the wrong behavior of your children and loved ones; and take care to be the first to carry out the word of God, before you teach it to others.

17.6.s.en: (3) His strength and the nations' submission to him

17.6.0.en: When God saw Jehoshaphat's faithfulness in his worship of God and his keeping His commandments, He blessed him and gave him awe in the eyes of all the kingdoms of the nations around him, so they honored him and feared him and did not try to fight him. Thus God fulfilled His promise that He spoke in the Law of Moses (Deut 11:22-25).

17.7.0.en: Burden: what an animal, such as a donkey or a mule, can carry on its back.

17.7.1.en: The nations did not only honor Jehoshaphat and hold him in awe, but also tried to appease him by bringing him gifts, so some of the Philistines brought a burden of silver and various gifts, and the Arabs brought seven thousand seven hundred rams and the same number of he-goats. The number seven signifies perfection, like the seven sacraments; that is, the nations offered complete love and submission to Jehoshaphat.

17.8.0.en: Jehoshaphat's activity appears in his building of castles beside the cities, and he also built store cities, to suffice for the needs of the kingdom of Judah. And this shows two things:

17.8.1.en: 1- God's blessing and support for Jehoshaphat.

17.8.2.en: 2- Jehoshaphat's greatness among the nations and his strength.

17.9.0.en: And Jehoshaphat's activity was not limited to what preceded in (v. 12), but he did many works in Jerusalem, which are not mentioned here in detail. And he prepared a strong army of mighty warriors to guard Jerusalem. The number of warriors in it was one million one hundred and sixty thousand, under the command of five skilled commanders. And one of them, Amasiah, is mentioned as having offered himself willingly to the Lord, that is, his heart was occupied with the Lord and he performed His service before serving the king. In addition to this, there was another number of soldiers whom Jehoshaphat placed in the various cities of Judah to guard them.

17.9.1.en: How beautiful it is to be active, doing your work with zeal and not being lazy, for you will receive blessings from God and feel happiness and succeed, and God will even give you awe and favor in the eyes of those around you.

17.9.2.en: We can summarize the characteristics of Jehoshaphat mentioned in this chapter as follows:

17.9.3.en: 1- Wise: in fortifying his kingdom, especially the northern cities facing the kingdom of Israel, so that the deviant religious thought of idol worship would not seep from Israel into his kingdom of Judah (vv. 1, 2).

17.9.4.en: 2- Keeping the commandments of the Lord and His worship: he refused the worship of idols and worshiped the Lord, like David, and kept the commandments of God (vv. 3, 4).

17.9.5.en: 3- Honored: God gave him stability in his kingdom and the submission of his people to him (v. 5).

17.9.6.en: 4- A teacher of the Law: he sent the princes, the priests and the Levites to teach the people the Law, so that they would be firm in the worship of God (vv. 7-9).

17.9.7.en: 5- Great among the nations: the nations feared him and did not fight him, but brought him gifts to appease him (vv. 10, 11).

17.9.8.en: 6- Active: he built castles and store cities and had many works to magnify Jerusalem, the capital of his kingdom (vv. 12, 13).

17.9.9.en: 7- Strong: he had a great army in Jerusalem and in all the cities of Judah.

17.9.10.en: Note: see the life of Jehoshaphat at the end of this book.

17.9.11.en: Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab to recover Ramoth-gilead
